story.head: The Kings shut down the dangerous stuff, the Sharks don’t
paras: The Sharks won the teams’ first meeting this season, 5-4 in overtime in San Jose on Oct 3. The Sharks (7-7-1) lost 5-1 to Ottawa on Saturday, and the Kings (4-7-2) lost 3-2 to Buffalo the same night. This is a Pacific Division matchup, with the Sharks fourth (tied for 19th in the NHL) and the Kings seventh (tied for 29th). The Pacific has been the weakest of the four divisions so far.

The Sharks’ record (.500) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.367), largely thanks to their goaltending. The Kings have played better than their record (.385) says: their chances are worth about .591, and their finishing has held them back.

The Sharks do a lot of their shooting from distance (2nd lowest), are one of the league’s most physical teams (2nd) and ice the puck a lot (32nd). The Kings leave the shooting to their forwards (lowest), lean on their stars as much as almost anyone (3rd lowest) and take a lot of low-quality shots (31st). The Kings keep dangerous shots away, but the Sharks give up a lot of them.

Macklin Celebrini (5 G / 11 A / 16 P in 13 GP) is carrying the Sharks’ offense, and Will Smith (6 G / 4 A / 10 P in 15 GP) has a team-high six goals. For the Kings, Artemi Panarin (8 G / 5 A / 13 P in 13 GP) leads the way in scoring, with seven goals in seven games against San Jose since 2023-24. Brandt Clarke (3 G / 7 A / 10 P in 13 GP) isn’t far behind.

Darcy Kuemper (4-3-1 / .878 SV% in 8 GS) will likely start for Los Angeles. San Jose has two options in net: Alex Nedeljkovic (3-2-1 / .899 SV% in 6 GS) and Yaroslav Askarov (4-5-0 / .900 SV% in 9 GS). They have split the last ten starts, and Nedeljkovic got the last one on Saturday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.

items.text: The Sharks have been without Igor Chernyshov and Alexander Wennberg for several games.
The Kings are newly without Adrian Kempe, have been without Alex Turcotte and Mats Zuccarello for several games, and have had to make do without Kevin Fiala all season.
Adam Gaudette has a point in four straight games against Los Angeles, with a goal in each of the last three.
Alex Laferriere has two goals on chances worth about 5.6 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
